next_question: After the runtime lane removes the first-20 locatableSample cap, does full DOM enumeration confirm that the a→link-inclusive page-type ordering changes between truncated and full-DOM, and does the null-model pairwise agreement exceed chance on full-DOM data?
why_next: This experiment's measurement is invalid (provenance mismatch: committed code does not reproduce stored results; estimator inflates bias ~4-7x by conflating total DOM counts with locatable counts). However, the directional finding — that first-20 document-order truncation introduces page-type-dependent bias that changes density-based ordering — is robust across both inflated and locatable-scaled estimators. The blocking substrate fix (locatableSample cap removal) in the runtime lane would provide true full DOM enumeration, resolving the estimator validity issue and enabling a reproducible measurement of the original scientific question (does truncation drive the 0.3 pairwise agreement and FALSIFIED verdict from EXP-INTEL-35112013458?).

established: First-20 document-order truncation introduces page-type-dependent bias in a→link-inclusive interactive density: ordering changes under both inflated-DOM and locatable-scaled estimators (product_listing vs detail swap for DEF-FULL-MAP; cart vs detail swap for DEF-FORM-ONLY) — robust across committed and stored analysis scripts (audit V1, V2)

Truncation discards 62-95% of locatable elements (82→20 listings, 32→20 details, 21→20 cart) with document-order selection bias confirmed by random baseline for a→link-inclusive definitions (DEF-FULL-MAP: mean trunc 0.2921 vs random 0.2888, 7/7 tasks random lower)

Bias magnitude is NOT 98% as a locatable-density point estimate — the full-DOM estimator inflates by using total DOM counts (393 <a>) instead of locatable subset (~19 <a>); proper locatable-scaled bound is ~69% listings, ~48-51% details, ~14% cart for DEF-FULL-MAP (audit V1)
On this truncated-first-20 sample (7 distinct tasks, 1 Magento site), the a→link mapping is sufficient to produce cart>product_listing>detail ordering identical to DEF-FULL-MAP (auditor verified)

Random ROLE_MAP null (1000 iterations, seed=42) on this sample produces mean pairwise agreement ~0.52, which is ABOVE the observed 0.3, falsifying the hypothesis that 0.3 exceeds chance (parent EXP-INTEL-35112013458)
rejected: Hypothesis that truncated-sample pairwise ordering agreement (0.3) exceeds chance-level expectation — FALSIFIED on this sample (null mean 0.52 > observed 0.3)
Hypothesis that no single-role definition produces invariant ordering — FALSIFIED: button-only and form-only both reproduce DEF-FORM-ONLY ordering (product_listing>cart>detail)
unknown: Whether full DOM enumeration (without first-20 cap) changes the null distribution shape, per-role densities, and ordering stability — the tag-count estimator used here is invalid as a point estimate (audit V1); true full enumeration needed via runtime substrate fix

Whether the product_listing vs detail ordering swap under full enumeration is statistically significant with adequate cart n and cross-site variance — current swap based on n=1 cart and n=3 per other type, means within 2% (inflated) or 0.016 vs 0.008 (scaled), no CI reported

Whether the committed analyze.py or the stored analysis_results.json is the canonical analysis — provenance mismatch means the script that produced the 3-definition per-role-filtered results is uncommitted (audit V2); must be resolved before re-run
Whether random 20 vs first-20 difference is document-order bias or sampling noise — observed Δ0.0033 (≈1%) with circular DOM-proportional pool; true locatable pool composition unknown
Whether menuitem/tab contribute additively when present (0 counts in this sample) — requires a sample where those roles appear
Whether the a→link reversal and ordering stability replicate on non-Magento sites or with different DOM structures (single-site bound)
do_not_assume: Do not assume the 98% relative bias is a valid locatable-density point estimate — it conflates total DOM counts with locatable counts; proper bound is 14-69% depending on page type and definition (audit V1)
Do not assume the FALSIFIED verdict from EXP-INTEL-35112013458 is fully explained by truncation — this experiment estimates ordering change but does not rerun the null ROLE_MAP test on full estimates

Do not assume C3 passes universally — it passes for DEF-FULL-MAP only; DEF-FORM-ONLY fails for all 7 tasks (random samples show higher bias than truncation for form-heavy definitions where form elements appear early in DOM)
Do not assume the stored result.json/analysis_results.json are reproducible from committed code — the committed analyze.py yields a different verdict (FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING) when re-run (audit V2)
Do not assume ordering differences between product_listing and detail are statistically significant — means within 2% (inflated) or 0.008 (scaled) with n=3 per type and n=1 cart, no CI reported
Do not assume the null distribution shape (0.52 mean, cart>detail>product_listing dominant) generalizes to other sites — bounded to this truncated sample from this Magento site
Do not assume the random baseline advantage (1% mean for DEF-FULL-MAP) is scientifically meaningful — it is within simulation noise (1000 draws, fixed seed) and definition-dependent
